what: The score combines exact insertion distance, a discounted best single 2-opt repair involving either new edge, a generalized-insertion radial reward, a feasible-neighbor clustering reward, and a mild residual-capacity packing penalty. It uses only the supplied distance matrix and performs O(len(route) + len(unassigned)) work per call, with O(len(route)) temporary storage.
why: Farthest-first route seeding benefits from continuing through customers in the same outer spatial region rather than immediately selecting cheap near-depot insertions, hence the radial and pair-savings terms. The capacity term mildly discourages choices that leave an unusable demand gap, which is useful when demands are heterogeneous, while remaining weak enough not to dominate geometry. The local 2-opt credit makes slot selection better aligned with the final post-construction objective. This is a non-admissible construction heuristic: its fixed weights are not empirically tuned here, the one-move 2-opt proxy cannot model interacting later improvements, and packing or clustering rewards can occasionally favor a locally coherent choice that is globally inferior.
